import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes for all features
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        effect = abs(feats.x[feats.y==1, i].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0, i].mean())
        effect_sizes.append((effect, fid))
    
    # Sort by effect size and take top features
    sorted_effects = sorted(effect_sizes, reverse=True)
    top_features = [fid for _, fid in sorted_effects[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # Check for strong correlations and remove duplicates
    final_drivers = []
    used_features = set()
    
    for fid in top_features:
        if fid in used_features:
            continue
            
        # Check correlation with already selected drivers
        is_correlated = False
        for existing in final_drivers:
            i, j = feats.column(fid), feats.column(existing)
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, i], feats.x[:, j])[0, 1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                is_correlated = True
                break
                
        if not is_correlated:
            final_drivers.append(fid)
            used_features.add(fid)
    
    # Use all features as columns
    columns = feats.ids
    
    # No products needed
    products = ()
    
    # Simple weighted score based on effect sizes
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        effect = abs(feats.x[feats.y==1, i].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0, i].mean())
        loadings[fid] = effect
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(final_drivers), 
                  columns=columns, 
                  products=products, 
                  loadings=loadings)
